**AMZN going into its Q3 2026 report: where things stand (as of Mon., Oct 19, 2026)**

**Resolution sources**
- My search didn't return the Yahoo Finance history page itself. Yahoo's main quote page shows a previous close of 250.00 (Fri., Oct 16) and an earnings date of Oct 29, 2026. Its 1-year analyst target is 331.46, YTD return is 11.11% and 1-year return is 20.38%.
- I didn't fetch the Metaculus FAQ. Its "credible sources" definition only matters as a fallback, with Nasdaq, Google Finance or WSJ standing in if Yahoo isn't available.

**Current price and recent action**
- Fri., Oct 16 close: $250.00, down 1.87% on the day. The 52-week range is 196.00–287.20 (Google Finance's figure for the high is $287.16). The beta is about 1.45.
- Mon., Oct 19: the stock rose sharply after Morgan Stanley named it a top pick and raised its price target to $350 from $335. Analyst Brian Nowak projected AWS revenue growth will accelerate to 47% in 2027. The gain also coincided with a wider technology rebound… following steep sector-wide declines the prior week. Intraday quotes were about $260 (+4%) at 10:26am and $262.60 (+5.04%) as of 11:06 AM Eastern. MarketBeat also shows a 50-day range of $245.96–$278.09.
- The stock started 2026 at $230.82.
- Last quarter's (Q2) results: revenue grew 19.6% year-over-year to $200.6 billion. GAAP EPS of $5.75 got a boost from a large one-time, non-operating income of $53.4 billion from the company's investment in Anthropic.
- Volatility: only 4 moves greater than 5% over the last year, so earnings days are where the big moves tend to happen.
- Valuation: P/E is about 20–21, the consensus rating is Moderate Buy, and the average target is about $322–331.

**Base rates (from my memory, not verified by search)**
- Over recent years, AMZN's typical move on the day after earnings has been about ±6–9%, and options usually price in roughly ±6–7%.
- Recent examples: about +10% (Oct 2025), about −8% (Aug 2025), roughly flat (May 2025), about −4% (Feb 2025), and a drop of about 5–10% in Feb 2026 on the roughly $200B capex guidance.
- The direction is close to a coin flip. Reactions depend heavily on AWS growth, capex guidance and Q4 operating-income guidance.
- From a base of about $255–262, a typical move would put the Oct 30 close at roughly $235–285. A larger 10%+ move would mean about $230 or lower, or about $290 or higher (a new 52-week high).

**Scheduled events before Oct 30**
- Big-tech earnings week: Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta are usually around Oct 28–29.
- The FOMC meeting is likely Oct 27–28 (check the exact dates).
- Amazon reports after the close on Oct 29.
- Ten trading days of general market drift come before the report.

**Status quo:** if the question were settled at today's price, the close would land around $255–262, which sits in the "$250 to <$265" bucket (if that's how the buckets are cut). The earnings move will most likely decide which bucket wins, and a typical-size move could easily push the price out of that one.

**Prediction markets:** I didn't find any Polymarket or Kalshi prices for this question.

letra_pequena: If Yahoo Finance is unavailable or does not report the value, the closing price reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) (e.g. Nasdaq, Google Finance, or the Wall Street Journal) for the same regular session will be used. Bucket boundaries are inclusive of the lower bound and exclusive of the upper bound (e.g. a close of exactly $250.00 resolves "$250.00 to less than $265.00"). If Amazon reschedules its Q3 2026 earnings report such that October 30, 2026 is no longer the first full trading session after the report, the question still resolves on the October 30, 2026 regular-session closing price. If U.S. equity markets do not hold a regular trading session on October 30, 2026 for any reason, the question is annulled.

(a) **Time left:** The outcome will be known at the close on Friday, Oct 30, 2026. That is about 11 days away, with roughly 9 regular sessions before the Oct 29 after-hours report and then the reaction day.

(b) **Status quo:** AMZN is trading around $260–263 intraday on Oct 19, up about 4–5% after Morgan Stanley's top-pick call and a tech rebound. If nothing changed, the close would fall in the "$250 to <$265" bucket, though near its upper edge.

(c) **Base rates:**
- **Earnings reaction:** AMZN's typical move the day after earnings is about ±6–9%. Options usually imply about ±6–7%, and the direction is close to a coin flip. Recent reactions were +15%, +1%, −6%, +10%, −8% and roughly flat.
- **Pre-report drift:** About 9–10 sessions of drift come first. With daily volatility around 2% (beta 1.45, and the sector has been volatile), that adds about ±6%. Big-tech peer earnings and the FOMC meeting also fall in that window.
- **Combined spread:** Together these give a standard deviation of roughly 9–10%, or about ±$25 around a center near $260.
- **Bucket probabilities:** A lognormal with σ≈0.10 centered at $260 gives about 16% / 19% / 23% / 19% / 23% across the five buckets.
- **Adjustment:** Earnings moves are fat-tailed: many reactions are small and a few are very large. I shift a little probability toward the middle bucket.

(d) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Downside:** Amazon guides capex sharply higher, toward $250B+, and AWS growth disappoints after the Q2 euphoria. The stock falls 10–12% to about $225–230, even though analysts are bullish.
- **Upside:** AWS re-accelerates past 40% with strong Q4 operating-income guidance, repeating the +15% Q2 reaction. That would push the stock past its all-time high to about $290–300.
- **Macro:** A sell-off across tech in the run-up week could drag the starting point down to the mid-$240s before the report even lands.
